customManagers.description: Track ICEBERG_V in versions.env. No built-in manager reads that file, so the Iceberg client jars were never updated.

packageRules.description: Patch, pin and digest updates run as soon as they are found. Holding a bug fix for up to a week gains nothing, and these updates are the ones least likely to change behaviour.
Flink stays on 2.1: Iceberg publishes iceberg-flink-runtime for 2.0 and 2.1 only, and fluss-flink has no 2.0 build. Raise this when Iceberg ships a runtime for a newer minor. See issue #9.
Fluss stays on 0.8.x because 0.9.x requires Flink 2.2, which has no Iceberg runtime. Moves together with the Flink ceiling above.

Spark stays on 4.1: Iceberg publishes iceberg-spark-runtime for 4.0 and 4.1 only, so a 4.2 image loads a 4.1 runtime and every Iceberg statement dies with IncompatibleClassChangeError. HADOOP_AWS_V in versions.env is matched to the Hadoop this series bundles, and the airflow image pins pyspark to the same minor. Raise this only when Iceberg ships a runtime for a newer minor, and move SPARK_COMPAT_MINOR, HADOOP_AWS_V and the pyspark pin with it. See PR #29.
Group all Python dependencies from pyproject.toml into a single PR
Group all Apache Airflow Providers into a single PR
Group Spark and PySpark updates together to prevent Py4J mismatches
Group the Iceberg REST catalog image with the ICEBERG_V client jars, because the catalog and the engine clients have to speak the same table format version
Group ClickHouse Server and Keeper to maintain cluster consensus
Group OpenMetadata Server and Ingestion with Elasticsearch. OpenMetadata only runs against the Elasticsearch version it was built for, so the three move as one set.
Group Marquez API and Web UI together
